overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated videos reveals a sharp performance split on FACTVERSE. Visceral 'What If You Fell Into...' second-person exploratory scenarios and extreme cosmic anomalies (such as TrES-2b, 55 Cancri e, and Venus's rotation) drive peak reach (800–1,050+ views) and highest engagement (up to 3.7% like rate). Conversely, generic psychology/brain trivia ('Fake Memories', 'Earworms') and duplicate uploads flatline under 100 views with negligible engagement. Pacing in the 19–21 second range consistently outperforms sub-16 second content.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Extreme Space Immersion
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dominate channel performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on sensory-rich, high-stakes 'What If' survival/immersion frameworks exploring terrifying cosmic entities.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' generated 981 views and 21 likes as the newest release; 'Planet Darker Than Coal' reached 1,029 views. Both maintained 19-21s runtimes.
winning_patterns.action: Select planetary and astronomical phenomena that present an immediate cognitive contradiction in the opening frame.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' flopped across three attempts (5, 10, and 53 views), while songs stuck in your head netted only 17 to 71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt standalone textbook psychology trivia; reserve neuroscience only for high-stakes micro-drama or dark mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads of 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' dropped from 220 to 34 views; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (12s) languished with 0-1 likes.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate direct re-uploads and enforce minimum 19-21s runtime with progressive narrative escalations instead of static facts.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Onto a Magnetar?
next_video.opening_direction: Instantly immerse the viewer falling toward a city-sized dead star, stating that within 1,000 kilometers, its magnetic field would dissolve their atomic bonds into microscopic threads.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that gravity accelerates your body to a third of light speed—so your atoms hit the crust with the kinetic energy of a trillion nuclear warheads, flashing into pure gamma radiation.
next_video.reason: Leverages the channel's strongest proven formula ('What If You Fell Into...') while introducing a fresh, unexploited cosmic phenomenon (magnetars/neutron stars) that combines extreme physics with visceral bodily stakes.
